summary: order-service's 5s+ p99 and 'ledger-db statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders)' errors are collateral damage from a code deployment in another service. portfolio-service dep-5905 (v4.5.0, deployed/rolled out 08:56:32Z) added an unindexed query over the 48.2M-row trades table on the SHARED ledger-db; a Seq Scan on trades (application_name=portfolio-service) began at 08:58:38Z, driving ledger-db CPU from ~30% to ~96%, connections from ~62 to ~190 and slow queries from ~1/min to ~140/min. order-service shares that database, so its INSERTs queued and timed out (p99 151ms -> 5607.8ms at 08:58; error rate 0.23% -> 9.43% at 09:00). Alternatives are ruled out: the DBA autovacuum change cfg-2903 was applied at 08:00Z yet metrics stayed flat for ~56 minutes until the deploy, and there was no failover/disk event (replication lag and disk flat) nor any order-service CPU/load increase. This matches historical incident HIST-111 (unindexed report query causing seq scans on ledger-db). Recommend rolling back dep-5905 or adding a covering index on trades(account_id, executed_at).

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service dep-5905 unindexed seq-scan query saturates shared ledger-db, starving order-service writes
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The new holdings P&L query shipped in portfolio-service dep-5905 (v4.5.0, 08:56Z) does an unindexed sequential scan over the 48.2M-row trades table on the shared ledger-db. This saturates the shared database (CPU ~96%, connections ~190, ~140 slow queries/min), so order-service INSERTs into orders queue and hit statement timeouts, producing the 5s+ p99 and ~9% error rate at order-service. Fault originates in the portfolio-service release.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5905 deployed 08:56Z adds new query on trades (account_id + executed_at), no migration/index
portfolio-service latency jumps to ~3.5-7s at 08:56 and its P&L query logs appear 08:59
ledger-db emits Seq Scan on trades (48.2M rows) slow queries from portfolio-service starting 08:58:38
shared ledger-db saturates: CPU ~30%->96%, connections ~62->190, slow queries ~1->140/min
order-service INSERT INTO orders hits statement timeouts, p99 ~150ms->5.6s, error rate ~0.2%->9.4%

assumptions: The 'trades' table seq-scanned by portfolio-service is the same shared ledger-db instance order-service writes to (both reference ledger-db; log shows application_name=portfolio-service on ledger-db slow queries).
order-service INSERT timeouts are caused by contention/queueing on ledger-db rather than an independent order-service fault (no order-service deploy exists).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Aggressive autovacuum config change cfg-2903 on ledger-db causes IO/CPU contention
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The DBA autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor change (0.2 -> 0.1) at 08:00Z made autovacuum more aggressive, causing IO/CPU contention on ledger-db that slowed all queries including order-service INSERTs.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: cfg-2903 was applied at 08:00:20Z but ledger-db CPU/slow-query/connection metrics stayed flat (~30%, ~1/min, ~62) for ~56 minutes until ~08:56-08:58, coinciding with dep-5905's rollout rather than the config change. The dominant slow-query pattern is an unindexed seq scan from portfolio-service, which autovacuum settings do not produce.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service capacity/resource saturation under load
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service ran out of its own capacity/resources (e.g. CPU or connection pool) under increased load.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: order-service CPU stayed flat ~40% and request_rate flat ~231 req/s (F11); the only load-linked metric that rose was db_pool_in_use, a downstream consequence of the saturated shared DB, not local capacity exhaustion.

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db infrastructure failure (disk/failover/I-OPS throttling)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: ledger-db suffered an infrastructure fault (disk exhaustion, primary failover, or I/O throttling) degrading all dependent services.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: replication_lag_ms stayed flat ~40ms and disk_used_pct flat ~71% throughout (F10), with no failover or connection-refused indicators; the degradation onset aligns exactly with a code deploy, not an infra event.

assumptions: portfolio-service and order-service both target the same shared ledger-db instance (dependency graph + portfolio-service's queries logged by ledger-db support this).
The 'trades' table seq scan (48.2M rows) is sufficiently expensive to saturate DB CPU and connection slots, which the metrics corroborate.
order-service has no other latent fault; absence of any order-service deployment and flat local CPU/load supports this.

timeline.event: Config change cfg-2903 applied on ledger-db (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2 -> 0.1); no immediate metric effect.
ledger-db slow_queries_per_min jumps ~1 -> ~139; CPU approaches ~96%; 'Seq Scan on trades' slow queries begin (first 08:58:38Z).
First order-service 'canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders)' error; error rate reaches ~9.4%.
Incident reported (order-service p99 > 5s with ledger-db statement timeouts).
Degradation still ongoing at latest data (order-service p99 ~5.2-5.7s, ledger-db CPU ~96%).

recommended_actions.action: Roll back portfolio-service deployment dep-5905 (or disable the new holdings realised-P&L query) to relieve shared ledger-db saturation.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5905's unindexed seq scan on trades is the verified trigger; rollback should restore ledger-db CPU/connections and stop order-service timeouts.

recommended_actions.action: Add a covering index on trades(account_id, executed_at) and/or make the P&L query index-eligible before re-releasing portfolio-service.
recommended_actions.rationale: The seq scan over 48.2M rows is the mechanism; an index converts it to an index scan and limits shared-DB impact.

recommended_actions.action: Add a pre-deploy query-plan review gate for queries against large shared tables (trades) on ledger-db.
recommended_actions.rationale: Same mechanism as prior incident HIST-111; a gate prevents unindexed seq scans reaching shared production data.

recommended_actions.action: Isolate/limit resource-heavy reporting queries from the transactional shared ledger-db (separate read replica or resource group).
recommended_actions.rationale: order-service writes were starved by a portfolio-service analytical query on a shared instance; isolation prevents cross-service blast radius.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT treat cfg-2903 as the cause; verify whether reverting autovacuum settings changes anything before acting on them.
recommended_actions.rationale: Metrics were flat for ~56 min after cfg-2903 and degraded exactly at the dep-5905 rollout, so the config change is not temporally causal.

data_gaps: No EXPLAIN plan/query text beyond the logged 'Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907)' fragment was available to confirm the index absence definitively; the conclusion rests on the seq-scan log line plus the deploy change description 'no migration included'.

No order-service-side metric finer than 120s buckets was available before 08:56; precise sub-minute onset alignment relies on ledger-db slow_queries_per_min (120s buckets) and portfolio-service latency (240s buckets) which agree at ~08:56-08:58.
ledger-db query_logs are truncated (360 of 360 WARN returned at limit) and were not fully enumerated; counts-by-pattern were used, which could omit rarer patterns.
No direct evidence of whether other consumers of ledger-db beyond order-service and portfolio-service were also affected.

findings.statement: config change cfg-2903 (ledger-db, autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2 -> 0.1) was applied at 2026-05-05T08:00:00Z / logged 08:00:20Z, ~56 minutes before the degradation began.
order-service has had no code deployment in the window (0 deployments for order-service, and the only deployment in the window was portfolio-service dep-5905).
ledger-db replication_lag_ms stayed flat (~40ms, max 43.67) and disk_used_pct stayed flat (~71%) throughout, showing no failover or disk-pressure event.

order-service's db_pool_in_use rose from ~14 to ~46 as its queries queued behind the saturated shared database; order-service CPU stayed flat ~40% and request_rate flat ~231 req/s, so load did not increase.
ledger-db is a shared datastore (owner platform, shared=true) used by order-service (edge order-service -> ledger-db, kind db) and equally by portfolio-service's queries appearing in its logs.
A prior incident HIST-111 (2025-05-22) had the same mechanism: 'New report query without index did sequential scans' on ledger-db causing slow queries and high DB CPU, matching the current pattern.
